CONCEPT A

Can-flipping robot · assembly manual · ME 2331/L

PART E

Electronics first: wire it flat on the table and test it while the parts print

E3
Bench test 2: one servo at a time (firmware/bench_test)

Plug only the servo for the next test. Brown = GND (rail −), red = + (rail +), orange = signal (pin). The MG996R's + / − go to the buck OUT terminals (cut extension), its signal to D9.

TestServoPlug signal toPress START, expect
☐1SG90 gripperD5Goes to 20°, wiggles ±10°, back
☐2MG90S wristD60°, wiggle to 20°, then a full half-turn 0 → 180 → 0: mark the horn and check it really reaches 180°
☐3MG90S liftD1030°, wiggles ±10°
☐4MG996R turntableD9 (+/− on the buck)135°, wiggles ±10°
☐5All four plugged in—All at HOME for 5 s. Meter on the rail: stays above 5.5 V

Each test: smooth, no buzzing, the Uno doesn't reset (no 3× blink in the middle).

E3b
Laptop control panel (viewer/control_panel.html)

1. Upload firmware/concept_a/concept_a.ino with the Arduino IDE, then close the IDE's Serial Monitor (only one program can use the USB port). 2. Open viewer/control_panel.html in Chrome or Edge (or the project site link). Click Connect to Arduino and pick the Uno's port. The Uno restarts; after ~2 s the angles appear. 3. Each servo has a slider, ±5° buttons and its working angles (base START 135° / TARGET 45°, lift DOWN / UP, wrist UPRIGHT / FLIPPED, grip OPEN / RELEASE / CLOSED). Every move is smooth and stays inside safe limits. 4. HOME brings the robot home one servo at a time. START runs the whole sequence (same as the physical button, which keeps working). START only runs from HOME. STOP (or Esc) holds where it is.

CheckExpected
☐Each servo buttonOnly that servo moves, to that angle, smoothly
☐HOMELift up → wrist → base → grip → lift down
☐START at HOMEGRIP → LIFT → FLIP → TURN → LOWER → RELEASE, ends DONE
☐START again after DONE (can removed)Goes home
☐STOP during a moveHolds; HOME before the next START

Tested without hardware: the firmware's commands on a simulated Uno (backend/tools/firmware_test/run.sh, 15 checks) and the page driving the live firmware through a fake USB port (panel_test.js, 11 checks).

E4
If something is wrong
SymptomLikely causeFix
☐Uno resets (blinks 3×) when a servo moves9 V battery flat, or the servo supply wired to the Uno by mistakeBattery < 7.5 V: replace it. Check nothing from the rail goes to the Uno's 5V or VIN
☐Servos twitch or don't respond at allNo common groundUno GND ↔ rail − (row 5b)
☐Servo buzzes / jittersSignal without ground, loose jumperRe-seat; shorter jumpers; ground first
☐Servo doesn't move at allSignal on the wrong pin, dead servoSwap the plug to a known-good test; try the spare
☐One servo works sometimes, then stops respondingCable / dupont joint (most often), power at its plug, or the servoSwap test (unmounted, horn off): plug that servo into a good servo's cable, and a good servo into its cable. Problem follows the servo → servo; stays with the cable / pin → wiring; both fine → it was a loose joint. Same code drives all four, so code alone is unlikely
☐Wrist stops short of 180°That MG90S's rangeservo_setup: try WRIST_MIN_US / WRIST_MAX_US 450 / 2550; else swap MG90S (buy a spare)
☐Rail below 5.5 V in test 5Weak adapter / long thin wires / no capacitorShorter rail wires; check the adapter is at 12.0 V under load; fit the 1000 µF
☐Buck gets hotPot set too high, shortUnplug, re-check OUT = 5.8 V with nothing connected
E5
Wiring dry run (decides what to return)

With the servos still loose, build the jumper chains (prototype v1 BOM): 2 jumpers per wire for the gripper, 1 for the wrist and lift, tape every joint. Re-run tests 1–5 through the chains.

• All pass, joints stay put when you tug and bend them → return the extension leads.
• A joint drops out or a servo resets → keep the extension leads.

Record the results (angles that looked right, rail voltage in test 5) in the build log: they go in the report's test section.

Then: PART P, printing, and PART M, the mechanics

Print plates A–E with the settings on the next page, fix up the fits, then follow steps 1–23. Keep the bench-test wiring: it moves into the tray in step 21.

P1
Printing: set these once (same for every plate)
☐Nozzle temperature235 °C (first layer 238 °C, never above 240 °C: PTFE-lined hotend)
☐BedTextured PEI sheet, 80 °C. No glue. Clean it with dish soap + water (or isopropyl) and don't touch the print area
☐Z-offseta little higher than for PLA: PETG must not be squished into PEI (it can stick too hard)
☐Removing partslet the bed cool to room temperature, take the sheet off and flex it: parts pop off
☐First layer0.24 mm high, 20 mm/s
☐Line width0.42 mm (0.4 mm nozzle)
☐Cooling fan30 %, off for the first 3 layers
☐Retraction5 mm at 40 mm/s (Bowden)
☐Solid / top infill speed40 / 30 mm/s
☐Travel speed150 mm/s
☐Max flowkeep under 8 mm³/s (stock CR-6 SE hotend): the speeds below already do
☐Elephant-foot compensation0.15 mm (Cura: initial layer horizontal expansion −0.15)
☐Seamrear / aligned
☐Skirt2 loops (unless the plate says brim)

Then print plates A → E (next pages). Each page shows what goes on the bed and the settings for that whole plate. Total about 24 h and 347 g of PETG.

P2
After printing: make the fits fit (sandpaper, drill, knife)
plate A
Must fit: it tests the fits
☐ Check each hole as in the build guide, section 2: it tells you how much to sand the real parts
plate A
Must fit: the 2 holes
☐ Peel the brim. Pivot screw binds: open the hole with a 5/32 in (4 mm) drill turned by hand
plate B
Must fit: 6807 bearing pocket (47.1 mm), MG996R screw holes
☐ Bearing tight: sand the pocket wall (120 grit on a finger) until it presses in with thumbs. Loose: one layer of tape. Clear support bits out of the servo pocket with pliers
plate B
Must fit: lift-servo screw holes, screw holes at the ends
☐ Run each screw in once and back out before final assembly
plate B
Must fit: 2 blind rod holes (6.0 mm)
☐ Rod won't go in: drill 6 mm, 8 mm deep (tape flag on the bit)
plate C
Must fit: nothing critical: board pegs, 2 screw tabs
☐ Peg too fat for a board hole: shave it with a knife. Snapped peg: a dab of hot glue holds the board
P2
After printing: make the fits fit (sandpaper, drill, knife) (continued)
plate D
Must fit: hub into the bearing (34.95 mm), 2 rod holes (6.0 mm), horn screw holes
☐ Hub tight: sand it evenly, turning it. Rod holes tight: drill 6 mm (or 15/64 in) by hand
plate D
Must fit: 4 LM6UU pockets (12.15 mm) in line, wrist-servo screws, link pivot
☐ Pockets print on their side, so the top of each droops: ream with a 12 mm drill or sandpaper on a 12 mm dowel / marker until the LM6UU presses in; the carriage must slide down both rods by its own weight
plate E
Must fit: gear teeth, axle bore 3.9 mm
☐ Remove supports, file only the pad area, never the teeth. Bore tight: twist a 5/32 in drill through by hand
plate E
Must fit: gear teeth, servo-spline socket
☐ Spline socket tight: scrape lightly inside with the knife tip, test the SG90 spline after every pass. Never file the teeth
plate E
Must fit: gear axle hole and servo position: they set the gear mesh
☐ Don't open the axle hole more than needed: the gears must mesh without play
P3
Fix-up rules

Tools: sandpaper 120 + 240 grit, 6 mm and 5/32 in (4 mm) drill bits turned by hand, a 12 mm dowel or marker wrapped in sandpaper, craft knife, flush cutters.

• Sand a press fit a little at a time, test after every few strokes. Too loose: one layer of tape or a drop of superglue.
• Never sand or file gear teeth.
• Plates B and C (coarse layers): holes can come out a little tight: drill or sand them.
• A part cracks at a screw: the screw was forced: drill one size bigger, use the next screw or hot glue.

Route: claw → wrist loop → along the arm → lift loop → spine window → down the back → turret notch → turn loop → base hole → tray. Tie at the tie points, leave the 3 loops free. Wrist loop ≥ 70 mm of cable.
